items.entity: Design domain Ω of the Fig. 1 example (shape / aspect ratio)
items.description: Sec. 2 says only 'An open domain with some volume fraction f is to be designed on'. The domain's shape and proportions appear only in Fig. 1, which is not available. The 64×64 square in Sec. 5.1 is stated for the dataset, not for Fig. 1. The example is assumed to be 2D.

items.entity: FE grid for the Fig. 1 example
items.description: Sec. 2 says only that the domain is 'discretiz[ed] ... into elements for Finite Element Analysis'. It gives no resolution or element type. Only the dataset (Sec. 5.1) is stated to use '64×64 ... square elements'. Because r_min is apparently in element units, the resolution also changes member size relative to the domain.
readings: aspect-matched grid, e.g. 128×64 Q4 elements for a 2:1 domain

items.description: ∂Ω_D appears only as a symbol in Sec. 2 and in the Fig. 1 caption ('a specific combination of boundary condition ∂Ω_D and load P'). Its location, and whether it is a full edge, a segment or points, is visible only in the figure. If Fig. 1 is a dataset-type case, Sec. 5.1 and Fig. 4 allow 1 to 4 of 16 options: 4 corners, 4 side midpoints, and 8 corner-to-midpoint half-edges. A single clamped node on its own leaves rigid rotation free, so a point support must be combined with other supports.
readings: entire left edge clamped (x = 0, 0 ≤ y ≤ H)
one half-edge segment, e.g. x = 0, 0 ≤ y ≤ 0.5H (dataset edge condition)
two corner nodes, e.g. (0,0) and (L,0) (dataset point conditions)
a side-midpoint node, e.g. (0, 0.5H), combined with a corner or half-edge condition
another combination of 2–4 of the 16 dataset conditions

items.entity: Point of application of force P
items.description: Sec. 2 says only that the domain is 'subjected to a force vector P'. Where it acts is shown only in Fig. 1. For the dataset, Sec. 5.1 places the load on a random boundary element.
readings: midpoint of the right edge (x = L, y = 0.5H)
midpoint of the top or bottom edge (x = 0.5L)
another boundary node/element as drawn in Fig. 1

items.description: The direction of P is shown only in Fig. 1. If it is a dataset case, Sec. 5.1 picks the angle 'from 0 to 2π ... from 6 evenly distributed values'. That could mean multiples of 60°, or linspace(0, 2π, 6), i.e. multiples of 72°.
readings: multiple of 72° (72°, 144°, 216°, 288°) if the 6 values include both 0 and 2π

items.description: Neither Sec. 2 nor the Fig. 1 caption gives a magnitude. Sec. 5.1 uses a unit magnitude for the dataset.

items.entity: Application of P on the mesh (node vs. boundary element)
items.description: Sec. 2 treats P as a single concentrated force vector. Sec. 5.1 says 'a random element along the boundary is chosen to be the load location'. It is unclear whether the force acts at one node or is shared among the nodes of a boundary element.
readings: concentrated force at a single boundary node
force split equally between the two boundary nodes of the selected element edge
force split over all 4 nodes of the selected boundary element

items.description: Sec. 2 says only 'some volume fraction f' and gives no value for Fig. 1. Dataset targets range from 30% to 50% (Sec. 5.1).
E0 appears only as a symbol in Eq. (1). Sec. 5.1 uses 'a unit Young's modulus' for the dataset's FE fields. Thickness is never given.
readings: physical value, e.g. E0 = 200 GPa, thickness = 1

items.description: Sec. 2 does not give ν. Sec. 5.1 states 'Poisson's ratio of 0.3' for the dataset's finite element field calculation.

items.entity: 2D elasticity assumption (plane stress vs. plane strain)
items.description: Neither Sec. 2 nor Sec. 5.1 says whether the 2D FE model is plane stress or plane strain. The choice changes the effective Poisson's ratio.
Sec. 2 gives E_min only approximately: 'a small stiffness (~0.001E0) to prevent errors'.
readings: E_min = 1e-9·E0 (common modified-SIMP default, if '~' means only 'very small')

items.description: p is introduced in Eq. (1) with no value in Sec. 2. Sec. 5.1 gives 'A penalty parameter of 3' for the dataset. Neither section says whether p is held constant or increased gradually (continuation).
readings: continuation from p = 1 up to p = 3

items.description: r_min appears in Eq. (6) with no value in Sec. 2. Sec. 5.1 gives 'a density filter radius of 2.0' for the dataset, without units (element widths or physical length).

items.entity: Filter weights w_ei (Eq. 6) and neighbourhood N_e
items.description: Eq. (6) writes w_ei = r_min − |x_i − x_e| with x as densities, so the weights depend on density differences. This contradicts the stated neighbourhood (distance-based) density filter. N_e is never defined.
readings: standard linear hat: w_ei = max(0, r_min − ||c_i − c_e||) on element-centroid distance, N_e = {i : ||c_i − c_e|| < r_min}
literal: w_ei = r_min − |x_i − x_e| (density-difference weighting) over a distance-based neighbourhood

items.entity: Filter implementation (which densities enter stiffness, volume and sensitivities)
items.description: Sec. 2 says density filtering produces a 'physical density' x̃_e. However, Eqs. (1) and (4) are written in x_e, and the filter is also said to 'distribute the effect of sensitivity calculations across multiple elements'. It is unclear whether FE and volume use x̃ with chain-ruled sensitivities, or whether the filter acts on the sensitivities or the design variables.
readings: standard density filter: Eq. (1) and Eq. (4) use x̃, sensitivities chain-ruled through the filter
sensitivity filter (Sigmund-type) on dc/dx, FE uses x
filter applied directly to the design variables after each update (x ← x̃)

items.description: Sec. 2 says only that x_e are 'updated using the gradient of the compliance, propagated back to the design variables'. Sec. 5.1 says 'a gradient descent algorithm'. Neither gives the update rule, step size or move limit, or how the volume constraint is enforced.
readings: Optimality Criteria with bisection on the volume Lagrange multiplier, move limit 0.2, damping 0.5 (top88-style)
MMA with the volume constraint as an explicit inequality
projected/autodiff gradient descent (fixed step or Adam), with the volume constraint enforced by projection/bisection or a penalty term

items.description: Sec. 2: 'iteratively updates the element densities until convergence is reached'. No tolerance or iteration limit is given.
readings: fixed number of iterations, e.g. 100 or 200

items.description: The starting design is never stated. Sec. 5.1 mentions an 'initial unoptimized domain' only for computing the stress and strain-energy fields.
Sec. 2 describes 'an open domain' and never mentions passive regions. Whether Fig. 1 contains any, or whether elements at the load or supports are kept solid, cannot be checked without the figure.
readings: none: the whole domain is designable
element(s) at the load application point fixed solid (x = 1)

items.entity: Definition of the compliance value c
items.description: Sec. 2 calls compliance 'the total strain energy in the system', but Eq. (2) defines c = UᵀKU (= FᵀU), which is twice the strain energy.
